Note::NlpAccessor::clean¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::NlpAccessor::clean() const

Establish A Conservative Text Baseline¶

clean() prepares untidy prose for later text operations without erasing its words, numbers, letter case, or non-ASCII vocabulary. It is the convenient choice when input has passed through editors, copied documents, or transport systems and several low-level artifacts need the same standard treatment.

The method performs these transformations in order:

Stage

Effect

Punctuation normalization

Curly quotes become straight quotes, dash variants become -, and the ellipsis character becomes ....

Control removal

C0 controls and DEL are removed, except tab, carriage return, and line feed, which proceed to whitespace normalization.

Zero-width removal

Known zero-width Unicode formatting characters are deleted.

Whitespace normalization

Runs of ordinary spaces, tabs, carriage returns, and line feeds collapse to one ordinary space. Form feed and vertical tab were already removed as controls.

Edge stripping

Leading and trailing ASCII whitespace is removed.

This is deliberately a conservative pipeline. It does not lowercase text, expand contractions, normalize numbers, remove accents, erase punctuation, or perform general Unicode canonicalization. Those choices can change lexical meaning and therefore remain explicit operations. For example, CAN'T and 1,250 survive cleaning unchanged.

Each cell is processed independently. The result is a newly allocated Text Note with the same rank, extents, and row-major cell order as the receiver; the receiver is unchanged. An empty Text Note remains empty with its shape intact. An undefined receiver propagates undefined. Bytes, Bool, Int64, and Float64 Notes are rejected before any cells are transformed.

The operation is idempotent: once its five invariants hold, applying it again does not alter the text. Use the individual punctuation or whitespace methods when only one stage is wanted, because clean() always applies the whole pipeline.

Example 1: Remove Several Kinds Of Transport Noise¶

const std::string dirty =
    " \t\xE2\x80\x9CShip\xE2\x80\x9D\xE2\x80\x94now\xE2\x80\xA6"
    "\xE2\x80\x8B\nnext\x01 ";
std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({dirty}).nlp().clean()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["\"Ship\"-now... next"]

The curly punctuation, zero-width space, line break, and control byte each exercise a different stage. The visible words remain.

Example 2: See What Cleaning Intentionally Retains¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"  I CAN'T pay 1,250  "}).nlp().clean()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["I CAN'T pay 1,250"]

Only the edge spaces are cleanup artifacts. Case, apostrophe, comma, and digits are content, so this method leaves them alone.

Example 3: Preserve A Matrix Rather Than Flattening It¶

const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{" can't ", "12", "“yes”", "plain"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(matrix.nlp().clean()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["can't", "12"], 
  ["\"yes\"", "plain"]
]

Example 4: Idempotence, Empty Input, Absence, And Dtype Failure¶

const auto once = matrix.nlp().clean();
std::cout << "clean idempotent=" << std::boolalpha
          << (once.nlp().clean() == once).all().bool_item() << '\n';
std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::string>{}).nlp().clean()) << '\n';
std::cout << "undefined defined="
          << pluss::Note::undefined().nlp().clean().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::bytes(
      std::vector<std::string>{"text"},
      std::array<std::int64_t, 1>{1}).nlp().clean();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "Bytes: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

clean idempotent=true
Note(shape=[0], dim=1, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]
undefined defined=false
Bytes: rejected

See Also¶

  • expand_contractions: expand a defined set of English contractions without performing general cleanup.

  • normalize_punct: run only the punctuation stage, optionally forcing ASCII output.

  • collapse_whitespace: normalize whitespace without changing punctuation or controls.
